name: Germanium point-contact amplifier
summary: Bardeen and Brattain pressed two close gold contacts onto germanium and obtained amplification, a solid-state amplifier that Bell Labs publicly announced as the transistor in 1948.
description: Bardeen and Brattain placed two closely spaced gold contacts against germanium to obtain amplification.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: Bell Labs wanted a solid-state replacement for vacuum tubes and relays in the telephone network, and earlier field-effect attempts had failed.
